I will keep my year simple and steady. In Quzhou, the system I trust most is winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That fits our weather, our water, and the way I know how to farm. At my age, I do not want a complicated mix of crops that needs too much watching or too much hand work. I will plant improved wheat seed because it is more reliable than old seed I save myself, and I will plant hybrid maize because hybrid maize usually gives me stronger yield. I will use moderate fertilizer, not too heavy, because I want stable growth and I do not want to waste money. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize, because wheat here depends more on timely water, especially after winter and around grain filling. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me than deep ploughing, and it matches the machinery work people usually arrange here. For pests and disease, I will keep applications limited and practical, only enough to protect the crop and avoid losing yield. I am choosing a wheat-maize rotation because it is the cropping pattern I know best, it spreads work across the year, and it gives me grain from both seasons with lower risk than trying something unfamiliar.
